high.title: SBV Determined to "Cool Down" Interest Rates
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) is facing multiple pressures in monetary policy implementation amid complex global economic and financial developments. Geopolitical tensions, particularly escalating military conflicts in the Middle East, have created significant pressure on international commodity and financial markets, with Brent oil maintaining an upward trend and raising inflation risks. Major central banks including the Fed, ECB, and BOE have maintained cautious policies and kept rates unchanged in early 2026 meetings, while some central banks like Australia, Ireland, and Philippines raised rates in the first 4 months. The strengthening USD creates pressure on exchange rates, interest rates, and domestic money markets. For FX traders, this indicates SBV's commitment to maintaining an accommodative monetary stance despite global tightening pressures, which could support VND stability but may create divergence with global monetary policy trends.

high.title: What Can Be Seen from SBV's Increased Monitoring of Commercial Banks' Interest Rate Reductions?
high.summary: The SBV's enhanced monitoring of commercial banks' interest rate reduction implementation demonstrates the central bank's determination to suppress the "silent" interest rate increases at some commercial banks recently, aiming to stabilize market interest rate levels to support businesses and citizens. However, given the complex and unpredictable global economic and geopolitical developments, with Vietnam's highly open economy, the SBV faces extremely challenging monetary policy implementation. The move reinforces SBV's commitment to maintaining lower interest rates despite global pressures, signaling continued monetary accommodation that could support economic growth but may create pressure on the VND if global monetary tightening accelerates.

medium.title: Unprecedented Event in Vietnamese Banking History: What's Happening?
medium.summary: Individual deposits in the banking system reached over 10.3 trillion VND by end-January 2026, the highest level ever recorded, increasing 0.45% from end-2025. This represents a 3.2 trillion VND increase from January 2025, while corporate deposits decreased 1.62% to just over 6 trillion VND. Credit growth reached 18.3% year-on-year by mid-May while deposit mobilization grew 14.9%, indicating strong credit demand relative to deposit growth.

medium.title: Expert Predicts a "Super Wave" of $50 Billion Could Hit Vietnamese Stock Market
medium.summary: ABS downgraded Vietnamese stock market growth outlook from "positive" to "neutral" after VN-Index fell 2.3% last week. Global bond yields have cooled after sharp early-week increases due to expectations of positive US-Iran agreements. Asian markets continue leading growth with South Korea's Kospi and Taiwan's TAIEX upgraded to "rising" status while Thailand leads Southeast Asian markets.

medium.title: Money Flow into Stocks Hits 2-Month Low, What's Happening?
medium.summary: VN-Index rose 9 points to 1,886 on May 25 but underlying market breadth was weak with 174 declining stocks versus 129 advancing. Trading volume reached only 13.9 trillion VND, the lowest in nearly 2 months since April 7. Market divergence shows investors remain cautious despite index gains, with liquidity concentrated in large-cap stocks while broader market sentiment remains weak.

medium.title: 14 Banks Reduced Staff in Q1, One Bank Has 1.5 Times More Employees Than BIDV and Over 2 Times More Than VPBank
medium.summary: Agribank continues leading with 40,579 employees as of end-2025, 14,578 more than BIDV and representing 56% more staff than BIDV. Total banking sector employment reached over 277,000 across 28 major banks, with the top 5 banks accounting for nearly half of total banking workforce. This reflects the continued dominance of state-owned banks in terms of branch network and employment.

medium.title: HoSE Announces 67 Stock Codes Cut from Margin Trading in May
medium.summary: HoSE added AAN (A An Food Corporation) to the list of stocks ineligible for margin trading due to less than 6 months of listing time. AAN officially listed on May 22 with a reference price of 15,000 VND per share and closed at 19,250 VND on May 25. The total number of stocks restricted from margin trading reaches 67 codes as of May 22, 2026.
